quests.instruction: A growing town needs new roads, parks, and homes, arranged so people can move around easily. Who plans how the town's space is used?
options: Estate Agent
Tour Guide
Urban Planner
quests.correctAnswer: Urban Planner
quests.hint: Think about someone who designs how a whole town fits together.
quests.explanation: Urban planners study how land is used and plan where homes, roads, parks, and services should go.
quests.funFact: Urban planners often hold meetings so residents can share ideas about their neighborhood.

quests.instruction: A city adds a new bus route so more people can reach the hospital and the market. Who studies where people travel and plans the routes?
options: Bus Driver
Transport Planner
Taxi Dispatcher
quests.correctAnswer: Transport Planner
quests.hint: Think about someone who studies how people move around a city.
quests.explanation: Transport planners look at where people live, work, and travel, and plan routes and timetables to match.
quests.funFact: Transport planners often count passengers to see which routes are busiest.

quests.instruction: A bus route is closed for repairs. Which people may have the most trouble getting where they need to go?
options: People without a car who rely on buses
People who walk to a shop next door
People who never leave their homes
quests.correctAnswer: People without a car who rely on buses
quests.hint: Think about who depends most on that service.
quests.explanation: When a service stops, the people who rely on it most are affected first, which is why planners provide other routes.
quests.funFact: Cities often arrange replacement buses so people can still travel during repairs.

quests.instruction: A main bridge is closed for repairs. Who helps drivers find another way?
options: Road workers placing detour signs
Bakers decorating birthday cakes
Tailors measuring wedding suits
quests.correctAnswer: Road workers placing detour signs
quests.hint: Think about who keeps roads organized.
quests.explanation: Road workers put up detour signs and barriers so that drivers know where to go instead.
quests.funFact: Detour signs often use arrows and bright colors so drivers can spot them quickly.

quests.instruction: Before a new restaurant opens, someone checks that the kitchen is clean and that food is stored safely. Who is it?
options: Building Inspector
Food Safety Inspector
Restaurant Waiter
quests.correctAnswer: Food Safety Inspector
quests.hint: Think about someone who protects people from unsafe food.
quests.explanation: Food safety inspectors check cleanliness and storage so that food does not make people ill.
quests.funFact: Inspectors often check that food is kept at the right temperature.

quests.instruction: A city makes a plan for what to do if a big flood happens: which streets to close, where people go, and who is in charge. Who writes such plans?
options: Event Planner
Lifeguard Supervisor
Emergency Planner
quests.correctAnswer: Emergency Planner
quests.hint: Think about someone who prepares for emergencies before they happen.
quests.explanation: Emergency planners think ahead about dangers and prepare plans so that services can respond quickly.
quests.funFact: Cities often practice emergency plans with drills so that everyone knows what to do.

quests.instruction: A water pump needs electricity. If the power fails, what might happen to the water supply?
options: It will start tasting like lemonade
It will always turn into solid ice
It may stop until power is back
quests.correctAnswer: It may stop until power is back
quests.hint: Think about how one service can depend on another.
quests.explanation: Many services depend on one another. If the power fails, a pump that needs electricity may stop until the power returns, unless there is a backup.
quests.funFact: Important water systems often have backup power so pumps can keep working.

quests.instruction: What might happen in a town if refuse collection stops for a long time?
options: Rubbish piles up and can attract pests
Streets become cleaner and cleaner every day
Trucks become lighter all over the town
quests.correctAnswer: Rubbish piles up and can attract pests
quests.hint: Think about what happens to rubbish that nobody takes away.
quests.explanation: Without regular collection, rubbish builds up and can attract pests and spread germs.
quests.funFact: Regular collection helps keep towns clean and healthy.

quests.instruction: When a new school opens, which services must be ready beforehand?
options: Only a new sign for the front gate
Roads, water, power, and safe buildings
Just one box of brand-new pens and pencils
quests.correctAnswer: Roads, water, power, and safe buildings
quests.hint: Think about everything a school needs before the first lesson.
quests.explanation: A school needs safe buildings, water, power, and roads before it can open, so many workers prepare in advance.
quests.funFact: New schools are usually inspected before students arrive.

quests.instruction: Who plans how a city's parks are cared for, including gardens, playgrounds, and trees?
options: Park Ranger
Parks Manager
Groundskeeper
quests.correctAnswer: Parks Manager
quests.hint: Think about the person who plans care for green spaces across the whole city.
quests.explanation: Parks managers plan how parks are looked after, organize staff and supplies, and decide on improvements.
quests.funFact: Parks managers often listen to residents' ideas about new play areas or gardens.

quests.instruction: Who in a local government helps keep official records, organizes meetings, and helps residents with forms?
options: Judge
Archivist
Town Clerk
quests.correctAnswer: Town Clerk
quests.hint: Think about someone who keeps local government organized.
quests.explanation: Town clerks keep official records, help organize meetings, and give residents information about local services.
quests.funFact: Records kept by a town can include maps, meeting notes, and decisions.

quests.instruction: Who designs and looks after the large pipes and pumps that bring water across a whole town?
options: Water Engineer
Plumber
Water Treatment Worker
quests.correctAnswer: Water Engineer
quests.hint: Think about the expert who designs the system, not the pipe fitter in your house.
quests.explanation: Water engineers plan and maintain pipes, pumps, and storage that carry water across a town. Plumbers usually work on pipes in buildings.
quests.funFact: Water systems often use gravity and pumps together to move water.

quests.instruction: Which set of services might all be needed after a big flood?
options: Lifeboat crew, road workers, power crews
Hairdressers, tailors, and cake bakers
Mountain guides, dancers, and actors
quests.correctAnswer: Lifeboat crew, road workers, power crews
quests.hint: Think about rescue, roads, and electricity.
quests.explanation: Floods can trap people, block roads, and damage power lines, so rescue teams, road workers, and power crews all help.
quests.funFact: After a flood, services often work together according to a shared plan.

quests.instruction: At a big sports match, traffic officers, stewards, and paramedics all help. What is their shared goal?
options: Winning the match for the home team
Keeping the crowd safe and moving
Selling as many match tickets as possible
quests.correctAnswer: Keeping the crowd safe and moving
quests.hint: Think about what all three jobs protect.
quests.explanation: Each worker does a different task, but all of them aim to keep people safe and able to move around.
quests.funFact: Large events usually have a plan that shows who does what.

quests.instruction: Why do emergency services share information with each other?
options: To avoid sharing anything at all
To give every worker the same job
To act fast and avoid repeated work
quests.correctAnswer: To act fast and avoid repeated work
quests.hint: Think about teams that need to know what the others are doing.
quests.explanation: Sharing information helps services respond quickly, send the right help, and avoid doing the same job twice.
quests.funFact: Emergency services often use shared radio channels or computer systems to stay in touch.

quests.instruction: Match these needs in order: building the stage, supplying power, removing rubbish, and giving first aid.
options: Paramedic, waste collector, stage crew, electrician
Stage crew, electrician, waste collector, paramedic
Waste collector, paramedic, electrician, stage crew
quests.correctAnswer: Stage crew, electrician, waste collector, paramedic
quests.hint: Think about each need one at a time.
quests.explanation: A stage crew builds the stage, an electrician supplies power, a waste collector removes rubbish, and a paramedic gives first aid.
quests.funFact: Big festivals can need dozens of different jobs working together.

quests.instruction: A hospital's night shift starts at 10 p.m. Why does it matter that some buses run late at night?
options: So buses stay empty at night
So hospitals can close early
So night workers can get to work
quests.correctAnswer: So night workers can get to work
quests.hint: Think about people who work when others are asleep.
quests.explanation: Transport timetables affect workers, so late buses help people who work at night to travel safely.
quests.funFact: Many cities run night buses to help shift workers and late travelers.

quests.instruction: Who brings neighbors together to plan a clean-up day or a new playground?
options: Community Organizer
City Event Planner
Town Council Clerk
quests.correctAnswer: Community Organizer
quests.hint: Think about someone who helps neighbors work as a team.
quests.explanation: Community organizers help people work together on shared projects and make sure many voices are heard.
quests.funFact: Community projects often begin when a few neighbors share an idea.

quests.instruction: A farmer's milk must reach a city. Which services does it depend on?
options: Only a brand-new door for the barn
One local radio station on the hill
Roads, trucks, and cold storage
quests.correctAnswer: Roads, trucks, and cold storage
quests.hint: Think about what keeps milk fresh while it travels.
quests.explanation: Milk needs roads to travel on, trucks to carry it, and cold storage to keep it fresh.
quests.funFact: Cold storage is used for many foods, not only milk.

quests.instruction: A big storm blocks a railway line. Which groups might be affected?
options: Commuters, delivery companies, and shops
Only the fish living in a small pond
Nobody in the whole town at all
quests.correctAnswer: Commuters, delivery companies, and shops
quests.hint: Think about who uses trains.
quests.explanation: People who travel to work, companies that deliver goods, and shops waiting for stock can all be affected.
quests.funFact: Railway workers often repair damage as quickly as possible so trains can run again.

quests.instruction: Why do cities inspect bridges, pipes, and power lines before they fail?
options: To make the bridges look much prettier
To fix small problems before they grow
To give inspectors something to do
quests.correctAnswer: To fix small problems before they grow
quests.hint: Think about preventing a big problem.
quests.explanation: Regular inspections find small faults early, so repairs can be made before they cause big disruptions.
quests.funFact: Preventive checks usually cost less than repairing a major failure.

quests.instruction: A town's tap water tastes unusual. Who should test it and tell residents what to do?
options: Water testers and health officials
Hairdressers and wedding cake bakers
Football referees and sports coaches
quests.correctAnswer: Water testers and health officials
quests.hint: Think about science and public safety.
quests.explanation: Water testers check what is in the water, and health officials give advice about whether it is safe.
quests.funFact: Water is tested often, even when nothing seems wrong.

quests.instruction: Teachers, caretakers, cooks, and bus drivers all help a school run. What does this show?
options: A school needs only teachers
Jobs outside school are unrelated
A school depends on many jobs
quests.correctAnswer: A school depends on many jobs
quests.hint: Think about everyone who helps a school day go well.
quests.explanation: A school day depends on teachers, caretakers, cooks, drivers, and many more workers, so every role matters.
quests.funFact: Schools often have staff meetings so that all these workers know what is happening.

quests.instruction: On election day, workers check names, hand out ballots, and count votes. Why must they follow clear rules?
options: So the result can be changed secretly
So the process is fair and trusted
So voting takes as long as possible
quests.correctAnswer: So the process is fair and trusted
quests.hint: Think about why people need to trust the result.
quests.explanation: Clear rules make sure everyone is treated fairly, which helps people trust the result.
quests.funFact: Election workers are often trained so that each step is done carefully.

quests.instruction: A new airport opens. Which jobs might be needed that did not exist in the area before?
options: Controllers, gate agents, baggage handlers
Only lighthouse keepers and ship pilots
Only deep sea divers and coal miners
quests.correctAnswer: Controllers, gate agents, baggage handlers
quests.hint: Think about what an airport needs to run.
quests.explanation: A new airport needs air traffic controllers, gate agents, baggage handlers, and many others, which creates new jobs in the area.
quests.funFact: A busy airport can employ thousands of people in many different roles.

quests.instruction: Two towns share a river. Why should their water engineers and environmental scientists talk to each other?
options: Rivers can never flow between two towns
Each town affects the other's water
Water engineers are never allowed to talk
quests.correctAnswer: Each town affects the other's water
quests.hint: Think about water flowing downstream.
quests.explanation: What happens upstream can affect people downstream, so towns that share a river need to plan together.
quests.funFact: Rivers often cross many borders, so neighbors share the responsibility for keeping them clean.

quests.instruction: After a flood, volunteers help paid workers. Why is that useful?
options: So paid workers can go home early
So fewer people are able to help
So more people can help with big tasks
quests.correctAnswer: So more people can help with big tasks
quests.hint: Think about big jobs with lots to do.
quests.explanation: Large clean-up tasks need many hands, so volunteers can support trained workers when there is a lot to do.
quests.funFact: Volunteers often receive simple training so that they can help safely.

quests.instruction: Which statement best describes a community system?
options: One person doing every single job alone
Many jobs meeting shared needs together
Jobs that never meet or share anything
quests.correctAnswer: Many jobs meeting shared needs together
quests.hint: Think about services like water, transport, and health care.
quests.explanation: A community system is made of many jobs and services that work together so people's shared needs are met.
quests.funFact: Good systems work because each part knows its role and shares information.

quests.instruction: Which chain shows how clean tap water reaches a home?
options: Treatment worker cleans it, engineer maintains pipes, plumber fixes taps
Plumber cleans it, engineer fixes taps, treatment worker maintains pipes
Engineer cleans it, treatment worker fixes taps, plumber maintains pipes
quests.correctAnswer: Treatment worker cleans it, engineer maintains pipes, plumber fixes taps
quests.hint: Think about cleaning, carrying, and then fixing.
quests.explanation: Treatment workers clean the water, engineers look after the main pipes, and plumbers fix taps and pipes in buildings.
quests.funFact: Clean water is tested at several points on its way to your tap.

quests.instruction: A storm hits a town. Which sentence shows good cooperation?
options: Each service works alone in secret
Only one service is allowed to act
Different services share updates and plans
quests.correctAnswer: Different services share updates and plans
quests.hint: Think about everything you learned about community systems.
quests.explanation: After a storm, many services help, so sharing updates and plans helps them work together well.
quests.funFact: Planning together before a storm makes the response quicker and safer.
